items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Ted Donelly and Henry Wells were nice trombone players and the reed section was quite strong.

ctx.x: "Big Jim" Lawson was a quite fellow who was quite big and must have weighed at least 200 pounds but he was solid and not fat. He could drink a lot and never show it, and was about the loudest blowing trumpet player I ever heard after Ted Colin. But he had a wonderful tone and although he could blow loud, it was not blasting.

Harold "Shorty" Baker was about four-feet ten and had one of the biggest sounds I ever heard from a trumpeter and he could blow quite strong also. He had a very personal style and was an all around trumpet player. I thought that I could blow fairly loud but I really had to put everything I could into my horn to be heard in the section. Ted Donelly and Henry Wells were nice trombone players and the reed section was quite strong. Buddy Miller played most of the first alto parts and Johnny Harrington played third…

Edward Inge I knew quite well because I had talked with him many times in Big John's bars and made some Redman recordings with him. Inge was a fine man who was always very conservative and never seemed to get excited or upset about anything. He was really the type of person that had complete control of himself at all times. He also played second tenor sax in some of the arrangement but he featured on clarinet.
